_readme: Phone compatibility for /check/. Only official, sourced lists. A model is never marked compatible unless the operator's (or Apple's/Google's) own page lists it. Anything not covered here shows 'check with your network'. No IMEI input, nothing is sent anywhere: the checker runs in the browser.

apple_carrier.label: Apple: About network operator-provided satellite features on iPhone
apple_carrier.rule: Apple says network-operator satellite features need an iPhone 13 or later with the latest iOS.

apple_sos.label: Apple: Use Emergency SOS via satellite on your iPhone
apple_sos.text: Apple’s own satellite features (Emergency SOS, and in some countries messages and Find My) work on iPhone 14 or later in {country}, separately from your network. They run on Globalstar satellites.
apple_sos.caveat: Not offered on iPhones bought in Armenia, Belarus, mainland China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan or Russia.

pixel_sos.label: Google: Get emergency help through satellite with your Pixel phone
pixel_sos.text: Google’s Satellite SOS (emergency texts only) works on your Pixel in {country}, separately from your network. Google says it covers every Pixel since the Pixel 9, except the 9a.

steps: Open Settings, then Mobile Data, then Mobile Data Options (or tap your network if you have two SIMs).
If you see Satellite there, your network offers satellite on your iPhone. If it isn’t there, it doesn’t (yet).
When it’s in use, the status bar shows SAT.
Open Settings, then Safety & emergency, then Satellite SOS, to see whether Google’s emergency satellite feature is on and to try the demo.
Network satellite services connect by themselves when there’s no signal and you can see the sky.
iPhone: signal bars, SAT and the network name T-Mobile SpaceX or T-Sat+Starlink.
Android: a satellite icon and the same network names.
